requirements_summary:
Regulated financial services buyer evaluating Redwood for internal RAG + lightweight agent workflows.

Primary requirements (non-negotiable):
- Deployment: Redwood Private in a customer VPC (AWS). Needs customer-managed networking and clear boundary between control plane/data plane.
- Security/compliance: audit logging, KMS integration, retention controls, and documented redaction rules. Wants reassurance that prompts, tool outputs, and retrieved content are not logged/exported by default.
- Observability: OpenTelemetry-compatible traces/metrics with low-cardinality attributes; needs correlation IDs (Redwood request ID) propagated into logs and traces for incident investigations.
- Template posture: “safe by default” (timeouts, retries/backoff, max token/cost caps) with explicit guidance on PII handling and prompt-injection considerations.

Nice-to-haves:
- Model pinning + rollback guidance (avoid surprise behavior changes); prefers Redwood-verified model list and a recommended fallback strategy.
- Prebuilt dashboards/alerts that can pass internal SRE review (avoid noisy defaults).

Risks/concerns surfaced:
- Telemetry tagging/headers: corporate proxies may reject unknown headers; requested opt-in design and documentation.
- Data handling: insists sample data in templates be clearly synthetic; no real customer PII in repos/log examples.

Current evaluation plan (draft):
- Phase 1: run template against synthetic docs in VPC, validate observability + redaction defaults.
- Phase 2: limited POC with scrubbed internal docs; measure latency/cost per answer + retrieval hit rate; validate audit trail for a compliance review.
crm_notes:
Account is highly sensitive to anything that looks like “logging customer data by default.” They asked directly: “Do your dashboards require us to ship prompts or document text to a third party?” Reiterated: OTel payloads must be configurable, with clear defaults and redaction guidance.

They are using a mix of internal proxies and security tooling that can break streaming and/or block custom headers. They want the quickstart templates to be resilient to disconnects and to degrade gracefully.

Key stakeholders on their side (names withheld in CRM notes): Director of Platform Engineering, Security Architecture lead, and Support Ops manager.

Internal owner notes:
- Pull in Allison Grant early for observability conventions + redaction processors.
- Coordinate with Product on a clear stance for template telemetry tagging being opt-in (and safe even when disabled).
- Make sure we have a crisp “audit-friendly log fields” section in the template README (request_id, model, latency, error_type, retry_count; no payloads).

Open questions to resolve:
- Data residency requirements (US-only vs region-specific) and retention duration for logs/traces.
- Whether they require SAML SSO for Console in the POC phase or only for production.
